newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-Atlantic spot power up on Pa. nuke outage.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-Atlantic spot power up on Pa. nuke outage.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the U.S. Mid-Atlantic climbed Wednesday on the unplanned outage of the 1,100 megawatt (MW) Peach Bottom 2 nuclear unit in Delta, Pa., late Tuesday, traders and brokers said.

Despite mild weather and modest electricity demand in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect district, the shutdown of the Peach Bottom unit triggered a jump in physical power prices, they said.
The unit had returned to full power Tuesday following adjustment to the reactor's control rods. PECO Energy today said the trip was caused by an electrical problem in the turbine generator.
PECO Energy Co did not provide a restart date for the unit, but industry sources estimated the plant would start up as early as Friday.
Firm, peak PJM electricity for Thursday delivery was quoted at $23.75-$24.75 a megawatt hour, up from Tuesday's range of $23.25-$23.50 for Wednesday delivery.
PJM electricity for the balance of October was quoted at $22.50-$23.50, sharply higher than $21.50-$22.50 on Tuesday.
November PJM electricity was assessed at $23.00-$23.25, higher than Tuesday's quote of $22.90-$23.20.
December PJM power was pegged at $27.00-$27.25, up from $26.90-$27.00 on Tuesday.
January/February 1997 PJM climbed to $31.00-$31.50, compared with Tuesday's quote near $30.75.
First quarter 1997 PJM was quoted at $29.00-$29.10, up from a range of $28.15-$28.50 on Tuesday.
Second quarter 1997 electricity delivered in PJM was assessed at $21.75-$22.25, flat from Tuesday's level.
July/August PJM deliveries were quoted near $31.35, up from deals done in the $31.10-$31.25 range on Tuesday.
